what_it_does: Intel SGX (Software Guard Extensions) is a feature in Intel processors that carves out a small, hardware-protected region of memory called an enclave — code and data inside it are encrypted and hidden even from the operating system. This paper focuses on finding software bugs inside those enclaves, which is important because bugs in SGX code can undermine the whole security promise. Existing automated bug-finding tools (called fuzzers — programs that throw random inputs at software to make it crash) only test the boundary where normal code calls into the enclave, and they do so in simulation rather than on real hardware. IntraFuzz is the first system that runs a coverage-guided fuzzer (one that tracks which lines of code have been executed and deliberately tries to reach new lines) directly inside a real, hardware-protected SGX enclave, so it can find bugs that only show up on actual hardware. The approach instruments the enclave code to collect execution-coverage feedback during fuzzing while respecting SGX's strict memory constraints.
